sections.body: The AI Researcher covers the places where artificial intelligence has moved into the daily work of scholarship, from reading the literature to running a lab. In practice this means tools that rank and summarise papers, extract claims from full texts, map who cites whom, and draft or check prose. It also means systems that help code qualitative interviews, clean quantitative datasets, assemble grant budgets, and schedule instruments. The site library holds 295 research papers and 14104 claims extracted from research works, which is the kind of raw material these tools operate on. None of this replaces a researcher's judgement, it changes what the judgement is spent on.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Search and summarisation are the most mature areas, and citation mapping is largely a solved discovery problem, though coverage gaps remain for non English and low resource fields. Quantitative pipelines are reliable when data is clean and the analysis is conventional, and they still fail quietly on messy or unusual designs. Qualitative coding assistants save time but their categories need human checking, and mixed methods work is only partly supported. Grant and peer review tools are useful for structure and consistency, not for judging importance, and integrity questions around authorship, disclosure and fabricated references are unresolved. The honest limit across all ten areas is that these systems produce plausible output, and plausibility is not correctness.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader starts with Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis for how papers are found, screened and combined, then goes to Citation Mapping and Discovery for the network view of who builds on whom. Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work and Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods split the analysis side by data type, with the second covering coding and integration of both. Grant Proposals and Funding and Academic Writing and Peer Review cover the production and evaluation of text, while Course Design and Teaching turns the same material toward students. Research Data and Repositories handles storage, sharing and metadata, and Laboratory Automation and Simulation covers the bench and computational experiment. Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity sits over all of them, because the rules about disclosure, authorship and error apply wherever the other nine pages lead.
